blocks.content: Retry Policies is the engineering practice used to define consistent failure recovery across providers and tools.

Define consistent failure recovery across providers and tools. In production, the hard part is not a single successful demo; it is building a contract that remains observable, secure, testable, and predictable under real traffic.

blocks.title: Core mental model
blocks.content: A retry policy must classify errors, cap attempts, budget time, and preserve idempotency.
1. What Retry Policies Solves

Retry Policies belongs inside a wider AI system. It receives a defined input, performs one bounded responsibility, and produces an output that the next stage can validate. Keeping that boundary explicit prevents prompts, provider behavior, and business logic from becoming one fragile block.

["Define the user or system outcome before choosing Retry Policies.","Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.","Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.","Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results."]
items: Define the user or system outcome before choosing Retry Policies.
Write down the input contract, output contract, latency target, and failure behavior.
Separate probabilistic model decisions from deterministic validation and side effects.
Keep provenance so outputs can be traced to inputs, model configuration, and tool results.

blocks.content: 2. End-to-End Architecture
A production Retry Policies implementation is a pipeline. Each stage should be independently measurable and replaceable.

["Classify work by latency and durability needs.","Assign an idempotency key and deadline.","Queue or batch compatible work.","Execute with bounded retries and backpressure.","Persist terminal state and notify the caller."]
items: Classify work by latency and durability needs.
Assign an idempotency key and deadline.
Queue or batch compatible work.
Execute with bounded retries and backpressure.
Persist terminal state and notify the caller.

blocks.title: Boundary rule
blocks.content: Every external response and model-generated structure must be validated before it enters trusted application logic.
3. Implementation Pattern

The example keeps the orchestration small and pushes validation, policy, storage, and execution into explicit services. This makes unit tests possible and prevents a provider SDK from becoming the architecture.
4. Production Failure Modes

["Using Retry Policies without a measurable success criterion.","Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.","Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.","Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.","Shipping without representative offline tests and production traces."]
items: Using Retry Policies without a measurable success criterion.
Allowing unbounded input, context, output, retries, or tool calls.
Assuming a valid JSON shape also means the action is authorized or correct.
Hiding provider errors behind generic retries until latency and cost explode.
Shipping without representative offline tests and production traces.

blocks.title: Least authority
blocks.content: Give the model the minimum context and the minimum set of capabilities required for the current request. Capability discovery must never silently become capability authorization.

blocks.content: Retry Policies is production-ready when its behavior is bounded, measurable, recoverable, and safe—not merely when the happy-path demo works.
